system.description: A small hand axe, useful as both tool and weapon.
Greek battle axe, also known as Epsilon. Can be wielded with one or two hands.
Greek battle axe, also known as Sapergis. Can be wielded with one or two hands.
A heavy two-handed mattock, primarily a tool but effective as a weapon.
A war hammer with a pick on the reverse, designed to pierce armor.
A wooden mallet, more tool than weapon but serviceable in a pinch.
Roman dagger, also known as Acinaces. Can impale.
Persian short dagger, also known as Pugio. Can impale.
A simple knife, useful for everyday tasks and close combat.
A curved dagger favored by Thracian gladiators.
Heavy leather straps with metal studs or plates, worn by gladiators.
Light leather wraps with minimal reinforcement for boxing.
A light mace, also known as Tukul. Effective against armor.
A light mace, also known as Garz. Effective against armor.
A heavy mace with a long haft, devastating against armored foes. Can be wielded with one or two hands.
A heavy mace with a long haft, also known as Garz. Devastating against armored foes. Can be wielded with one or two hands.
A simple wooden club, the weapon of the poor.
A heavy work maul, cumbersome but powerful.
Small shield or buckler, also known as Pelta.
Small shield or buckler, also known as Parmula.
Medium-sized shield, also known as Telamon.
Medium-sized shield, also known as Parma.
Large Roman shield, light for its size.
Heavy Greek hoplite shield, also known as Clipaeus.
Heavy Roman shield, also known as Aspis.
A basic large shield without metal rim reinforcement.
Roman short spear. Can be wielded with one or two hands. Can impale.
Heavy Roman javelin with long metal shank, also known as Falarica. Can be used in melee or thrown. Can impale.
Heavy Iberian javelin with long metal shank, also known as Pilum. Can be used in melee or thrown. Can impale.
Iberian all-metal javelin, also known as Saunion. Feared for armor penetration. Can be used in melee or thrown. Can impale.
Iberian all-metal javelin, also known as Soliferrum. Feared for armor penetration. Can be used in melee or thrown. Can impale.
A fishing trident, improvised as a weapon.
War trident used by gladiators, heavier and more deadly than fishing tridents.
Standard javelin, also known as Gabalum. Can be used in melee or thrown. Can impale.
Standard javelin, also known as Veretum. Can be used in melee or thrown. Can impale.
Greek long spear, the primary weapon of hoplites. Can impale.
Heavy cavalry lance. Cannot parry. Can only be used from horseback. Can impale.
Macedonian pike, 4-6 meters long. Pike block only. Can impale.
Iberian curved sword, also known as Kopis or Machaeira. Can impale.
Greek curved sword, also known as Falcata or Machaeira. Can impale.
Greek curved sword, also known as Falcata or Kopis. Can impale.
Short Dacian curved sword, also known as Harpe. Can impale.
Greek curved sword, also known as short Falx. Can impale.
Agricultural hedging hook, improvised as a weapon.
Roman short sword, also known as Xiphos or Acinaces. Can impale. Does 1d6+1 when cutting.
Greek short sword, also known as Gladius or Acinaces. Can impale. Does 1d6+1 when cutting.
Persian short sword, also known as Gladius or Xiphos. Can impale. Does 1d6+1 when cutting.
Egyptian sickle-sword with distinctive hooked blade.
Roman cavalry sword, longer than the gladius. Can impale.
Farming sickle, improvised as a weapon. Can impale.
Long Dacian two-handed curved sword, also known as Rhomphaia. Can impale.
Thracian two-handed curved sword, also known as long Falx. Can impale.
Farming flail improvised as a weapon.
Farming hoe used as an improvised weapon.
Farming scythe, deadly when improvised as a weapon. Can impale.
Digging spade used as an improvised weapon.
Powerful recurved bow made from horn, wood, and sinew. Can impale.
Tall self bow made from a single piece of wood. Can impale.
Small bow suitable for hunting and skirmishing. Can impale.
Heavy steel crossbow with windlass. Devastating power but slow to reload. Can impale.
Light crossbow, easier to reload than heavier versions. Can impale.
Small throwing dart. Can impale.
Lead-weighted barbed dart, also known as martiobarbuli. Can impale.
Sling with molded lead bullets. Best mix of range and damage.
Sling with simple stones. Less effective than lead bullets.
Two-handed staff sling for shooting heavier payloads.
Roman two-handed staff sling for shooting heavier payloads.
A rock thrown one-handed. Gains +1d6 per 3m elevation above target.
Large rock thrown two-handed. Gains +1d6 per 3m elevation. Subtract 1% per meter above target.
Gallic throwing weapon like a boomerang, reinforced with metal bands.
Greek throwing stick like a shepherd's crook, used primarily for hunting.
Flung noose used by Sagartians and Laquearius gladiators. Entangles target.
Combat net used by Retarius gladiators. Entangles target.
